title: Workspace suggestion result
description: What a run answers. Three statuses and all of them are answers: a refusal is a successful classification rather than a failure, and an exhausted run still carries what it composed. Deliberately absent: prices, names and images - the application resolves those from its own catalogue and recomputes every amount, so a language model can never influence a charge - and any sentence the model wrote, which is why criteria are tokens.

status.description: ok: the reviewer approved. exhausted: three attempts spent and still unapproved, so the candidates travel with the findings against them. rejected: the verifier judged this not a workspace request.

code.description: Present when status is rejected. The application maps it to its own words; the agent never sends the sentence.

options.description: Empty when rejected. Otherwise one per budget tier, in the order low, middle, high.

findings.description: What the reviewer objected to, present when status is exhausted. Structured rather than prose, so the application renders it.

lines.description: What fills each slot. SKUs and quantities only: the application resolves the name, the image and the price.

criteria.description: The criteria this option satisfies, as closed-vocabulary tokens rather than sentences: 'slot:chair', 'quantity:monitor:2', 'tag:standing', 'attribute:desk:type:sit-stand'.

unevaluated.description: Criteria the catalogue cannot express, carried rather than dropped. The phrase is the customer's own word, quoted; it is the only free text in this contract and it comes from the request, never from the model.

pinnedSlots.description: Slots with fewer than three candidates, where the same product fills every tier and the tier therefore means nothing for that slot.
